newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU group to air "best-practice" transport taxation.
newsitem.headline: EU group to air "best-practice" transport taxation.

text.p: European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock agreed on Monday to launch a working group with industry and environmental groups to establish best-practice suggestions to tax transport according to the damage it causes.

The idea would be to develop pricing systems, in the form of charges and taxes, to encourage low-impact means of transport at the expense of ones which cause more pollution, infrastructure damage or congestion.

Not only should such systems differentiate between modes but also between the technical capabilities of chosen vehicles in any mode, according to the Commission's green paper on transport pricing, COM(95)691. Thus an ideal system would make state-of-the-art, low-emission lorries pay less than older, more polluting ones.

"On present trends and with continued reliance solely on current policies, several significant, existing threats to commercial and personal mobility will simply get worse," Kinnock said in a speech to a Commission-sponsored conference called "Fair and Efficient Pricing in Transport".

"Congestion is obviously a particular and growing menace. If an effective and comprehensive strategy is not urgently phased in, transport thrombosis will continue to spread. That will generate even higher costs than today's estimated two percent of gross domestic product," he said.

The Commission plans during the coming weeks to propose a non-binding framework outlining how such ideas could apply to airport landing and use charges, favouring for example, quiet, less-polluting aircraft over others.
Similar plans, adopted already or in the Commission works, tackle differentiation in road haulage pricing, charges for railway infrastructure use and port charges for oil tankers.
Kinnock agreed the plan after a one-day symposium involving Commission and Council officials and representatives from the many interest groups which make up Europe's transport lobby.
